content.title: March Madness 2026: Start time, TV schedule, live stream for Selection Sunday NCAA bracket release
content.text: LET THE MADNESS BEGIN! For the first time in TCU history both the Horned Frogs Men’s & Women’s Basketball programs will participate in the NCAA Tournament during the same season. Where will TCU begin their roads to the Final Four when the bracket is announced on Selection Sunday?How to watch: 2026 Men’s NCAA Tournament Selection ShowStart Time: Sunday, March 15 | 5:00 PM CentralTV Broadcast: CBSStreaming Broadcast: Paramount+Live Stream: NCAA March Madness LiveTCU Men’s Basketball had an incredible surge to close the regular season and is playing some of its basketball headed into the NCAA Tournament despite a tough loss to the Kansas Jayhawks in the Big 12 Tournament Quarterfinals. The Frogs opened the season with a baffling home loss to New Orleans, but has delivered the best performance in conference play since joining the Big 12. TCU delivered six elite Quadrant 1 wins and have a resume ranked 38th in the NET, 35th in Strength of Record, and 33rd in Wins Above Bubble. When the bracket is revealed on Selection Sunday, the Horned Frogs are very likely to be slotted in as a No. 8 or No. 9 seed, where a win would mean a likely showdown with one of the elite No. 1 seeds in the Second Round. While that makes a Cinderella run to the National Championship, TCU is set at +50,000 to cut the nets in Indianapolis, per FanDuel Sportsbook. Potential First Round matchups include the Ohio State Buckeyes, Saint Louis Billikens, Clemson Tigers, and Villanova Wildcats. The First Round will be played March 19 & 20 in Buffalo NY, Greenville SC, Oklahoma City OK, Portland OR, Tampa FL, Philadelphia PA, San Diego CA, and St. Louis MO.How to watch: 2026 Women’s NCAA Tournament Selection ShowStart Time: Sunday, March 15. | 7:00 PM CentralTV Broadcast: ESPNStreaming Broadcast: WatchESPN / / ESPN AppLive Stream: NCAA March Madness LiveThe rise of TCU Women’s Basketball under head coach Mark Campbell continues. After leading the Horned Frogs to its first ever Elite Eight appearance last season, in 2026 TCU repeated as Big 12 regular season champions before falling in the Title Game of the Big 12 Tournament. Dazzling point guard Olivia Miles was named Big 12 Player of the Year and Newcomer of the Year, the second consecutive Horned Frog to win both awards, following Hailey Van Lith in 2025. TCU forward Marta Suarez joined Miles as unanimous All-Big 12 First Team selections. With the Women’s bracket, the top-16 seeds are hosts for the First & Second Rounds and are announced ahead of Sunday’s full bracket reveal, albeit without confirming exact seeds for each. TCU will officially host in Schollmaier Arena after being named one of the top seeds on Saturday. TCU could potentially be designated as high as a No. 2 seed when the bracket is revealed, but falling in the Big 12 Championship likely locks the Horned Frogs in as a 3-seed, which would likely prevent TCU from landing in a pod that ends up in a Fort Worth Regional, hosted at Dickies Arena. The other pair of Regionals (Sweet Sixteen & Elite Eight) will be held in Sacramento, CA.0 Comments
